audio.note: It DISPROVED my hypothesis before trusting it: muting the whole pa bus left the hiss intact and the speech bus reads exact digital silence when closed, so the round-3 open-channel hiss was properly gated all along. PA had two causes in audio: echoCancellation on speakers (Chrome's AEC references the page's own render stream, which contains the player's voice returning from the ceiling 10-200ms later - it was subtracting the thing it was protecting), and the voice arriving at parity with the bed so opening the channel made the mix 4.3 dBA QUIETER because the two ducks outweighed the voice they made room for. THIRD BUG found while validating: the howl watchdog had never fired and COULD not - it read the output of a 6:1 compressor thresholded at -26dBFS against 0.30 linear, which needs +85dBFS at its input. Rebuilt on the raw mic with a steadiness discriminator, because level alone cannot separate a shout from a howl.
audio.verdict: PASS on both bugs. HISS: airTop in bed.js used filt('highshelf', 5200, 0.7, 6) on pink noise - pink falls 3dB/octave, so a +6dB shelf spanning two octaves flattens it EXACTLY, generating WHITE noise above 5kHz, which is the definition of tape hiss. 11.2kHz band went -46.6 -> -69.8dB while everything below 5.6kHz moved under 2dB.

camera.note: THE BUG IT NEARLY SHIPPED, and caught with its own sweep: the decoupling was a fiction at exactly the angles it was bought for. Round 1 reads yaw back off the POSED camera, justified by a lateral residual between eye and aim worth 1.5 degrees across a 5.55m boom. The glance dolly takes that boom to 1.15m, where the same 0.15m residual is 7 degrees - and a spring half a metre behind a moving cop is fifty. So a deep glance WAS steering the player, through a trigonometric side door rather than the axis latch. Its own words: 'everything I wrote you about the loop being closed depended on that being zero.' Fixed by computing moveYaw analytically off the UNDOLLIED boom; both terms are no-ops at zero look so the mouse-idle frame is round 1 to the bit. It judged the HUD brackets with the RENDERER rather than arithmetic - marker pixels isolated with a difference frame against projectFromCop - and the worst error bucket is the one with no look in it.
camera.verdict: PASS. Mouse look with a 110-degree budget, movement decoupled. Builder's own proofs: yaw truthful to 0.00000 degrees over 2160 checks, moveYaw invariant to 0.00000 while the boom ran 5.57 -> 1.15m, HUD brackets median 2.2px and FLAT by look bucket.

THE BUG IT NEARLY SHIPPED, and caught with its own sweep: the decoupling was a fiction at exactly the angles it was bought for. The glance dolly takes that boom to 1.15m, where the same 0.15m residual is 7 degrees - and a spring half a metre behind a moving cop is fifty. So a deep glance WAS steering the player, through a trigonometric side door rather than the axis latch. Its own words: 'everything I wrote you about the loop being closed depended on that being zero.' Fixed by computing moveYaw analytically off the UNDOLLIED boom; both terms are no-ops at zero look so the mouse-idle frame is round 1 to the bit. It DISPROVED my hypothesis before trusting it: muting the whole pa bus left the hiss intact and the speech bus reads exact digital silence when closed, so the round-3 open-channel hiss was properly gated all along. Rebuilt on the raw mic with a steadiness discriminator, because level alone cannot separate a shout from a howl.

Root cause was NOT the avoid radius: nav.steer did greedy descent FIRST then filtered, so a corked aisle fouled every point, got=false, and it fell back to 'furthest visible point' — the far side of the cop. The thief sprinted INTO him. Fix prices the cop as a cost inside the Dijkstra flood, but ONLY downstream of the runner: without that filter a cop merely behind prices the ground the thief stands on and the stern chase leaks 1.3% -> 79%.

Confirms the coupling I flagged: observer catch fell 79.4% -> 59.7% once the chase stopped being unlosable, and points fell 1532 -> 912. The old figure was inflated by a chase that auto-caught. The skill separation survives the correction, which is the result that matters.

COUNTERPLAY: the cop is now a COST IN THE ESCAPE FLOOD, not a filter on an already-computed descent. Root cause of the cork: nav.steer's avoid ran AFTER a greedy gradient walk, so it could only pick a nearer point on the same line -- when every point was fouled it fell back to the far side of the cop and the thief sprinted into him. Threat now enters the Dijkstra cost (nav.field opt.avoid), gated to cells downstream of the runner so a pursuer behind him never bends his route. Plus: thief reacts when he SEES the aisle mouth blocked (8.6m, needs LOS + on his route line) instead of walking to 4.5m; tangential (not radial) cop avoidance while running; a committed shoulder-barge whose outcome depends on where the cop was standing when he committed -- hold the lane centre and you have him, drift off one side and he goes past the other for the price of a 0.45s stumble. Per-thief nerve so the route decision is not a pure function of position.
